clue.text: Torn-up shoestring subjected to review

blocks.note: a shoestring is a shoelace, or lace
something reviewed has been rated or assessed

explanation.surface: A tattered, cheap production gets panned by the critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoestring' suggests a tiny budget, but here it is the literal lace in a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerated flesh or material is ripped and gashed, the same as torn up.

clue.text: Fish, see, feels pain

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look or see
someone who aches feels pain

explanation.surface: A sympathetic plea that fish really do suffer when caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaches are small freshwater fish, popular in aquariums, so the plural noun matches the plural sense of the noun.

clue.text: Churned ice stream is smoother than all others

indicators.note: churning stirs and beats things about, so the letters get mixed into new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Churned ice cream, flowing like a stream, is the silkiest dessert of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churned ice' points to ice cream, which fits the definition's texture nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of creamy describes the richest, most velvety texture, i.e. the smoothest one.

clue.text: Once again, add a bit of experience for curriculum vitae

indicators.note: a bit is just a small piece, here the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to sum is to add up
first letter of experience

explanation.surface: Advice to job hunters: keep topping up the CV with more experience.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US a résumé is the usual word for a CV.
explanation.definitionFit: A résumé is the American name for the document summarising a career, the same thing a British CV is.

clue.text: Loud, grand claims under suspicion at first

indicators.note: to claim something is to take it in as one's own, so one piece holds another
at first points to the opening letter of the preceding word only

blocks.note: a thou, short for thousand, is slang for a grand
taken as written
first letter of suspicion

explanation.surface: Bold, loudly made claims are now being doubted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under suspicion' reads as a phrase, but under is a separate word that goes inside the slang for a grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunderous applause or a thunderous voice is extremely loud, like a roll of thunder.

clue.text: Obligation extracted from last Bedouin upon returning

indicators.note: extracted from means pulled out of the run of letters in the following words
returning means going back, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A duty owed to the final nomad on their return to camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is something owed, a duty to pay back, which is a kind of obligation.

clue.text: God's way to tell a mug from a demitasse?

blocks.note: a mug and a demitasse are both kinds of cup
ID, identification, is how you tell one thing from another

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about how a deity distinguishes big coffee vessels from tiny ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase reads as 'cup ID', a way to identify a cup; the question mark flags this playful reading. A demitasse is a small coffee cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid is the Roman god of love, so he is a god.

clue.text: Drug may snatch lives

blocks.note: can and may both express permission
to nab is to grab or snatch
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A warning that a narcotic can take lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' looks like a noun, as in deaths; it is the verb, meaning exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is the plant-based drug also called marijuana.

clue.text: Parts of a kingdom covered by pornography laws

indicators.note: something covered by other material sits concealed inside it

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Some regions of a realm fall under obscenity legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kingdom' suggests a country, but in biology the animal and plant kingdoms are divided into phyla.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification each kingdom is subdivided into phyla, the rank just below it.

clue.text: Cruise had brought up flowers

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up means reading it from the bottom upward

blocks.note: to cruise is to sail
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tom Cruise raised some blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruise' with a capital letter suggests the actor Tom Cruise; it is the verb, to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahlias are showy garden plants grown for their blooms, so they are flowers.

clue.text: Helps Japanese prime minister with empty threats

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: Shinzo Abe was Prime Minister of Japan
outer letters of threats

explanation.surface: Diplomatic support for a Japanese leader who makes hollow threats.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, usually in wrongdoing, so abets means gives help to.

clue.text: Run my bath? That's crazy — say there are alligators in the sewers

definitions.text: say there are alligators in the sewers
definitions.note: a definition by example: the alligator story is one such tale

indicators.note: something crazy is deranged and out of order, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a bath, given the rumour of alligators lurking in the drains below.
explanation.walkthrough: The alligators-in-the-sewers story about New York is the textbook example; 'say' signals an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban myth is a widely repeated but untrue modern story, and the sewer alligators tale is a classic instance.

clue.text: DIY garden tool is getting me angry

indicators.note: getting here means receiving or taking in, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: a hoe is a garden tool for weeding
taken as written
mad means angry

explanation.surface: A frustrated gardener grumbles about a do-it-yourself tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'DIY garden tool' reads as one phrase; DIY is in fact the definition, standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: DIY, do-it-yourself, describes things you make yourself at home, which is what homemade means.

clue.text: Middle Eastern queen: an electronics pioneer

blocks.note: Q is the abbreviation for queen, as in chess
Atari was a pioneering video game and home computer company

explanation.surface: A queen from the Arab world turns out to be a technology trailblazer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pioneer' suggests a person, but it is a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Qatari means belonging to Qatar, a Gulf state, so it is an adjective for something from that region.

clue.text: Volunteer group singing printed music about green vegetables?

indicators.note: singing is voicing words out loud, so the clue goes by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: peas are small green vegetables
a score is music written down

explanation.surface: A volunteer choir performs from sheet music about vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'peas score' would be a piece of music about peas; said out loud it runs together into the answer. The Peace Corps is the US government's overseas volunteer programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peace Corps is an American agency that sends volunteers abroad, so it is a body of volunteers.

clue.text: That woman would lose small storage structure

blocks.note: a third meaning: ..., the contraction of she would, written without the apostrophe
first meaning: to cast off, as a snake does its skin
second meaning: a hut in the garden for tools

explanation.walkthrough: This is really a triple definition: the contraction for 'she would', a verb for losing something, and a garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed leaves or skin is to lose them, and a shed is a small outbuilding used for storage.

clue.text: Indigenous Canadians accepting trees' eerie quality

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one part is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the Cree are a First Nations people of Canada
pines are a kind of tree

explanation.surface: A First Nations community embraces the spooky atmosphere of the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepiness is the unsettling, spooky feeling of something that makes your skin crawl, i.e. eeriness.

clue.text: Men, pacing all around and putting up tents

indicators.note: pacing all around suggests wandering in every direction, so the letters go out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Restless men walk about while pitching their tents.
explanation.definitionFit: Encamping means setting up a camp, which involves pitching shelters for the night.

clue.text: Farm animal (a pig) decapitated by fellow laborer

indicators.note: decapitated means beheaded, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a cow is a farm animal
a porker is a pig

explanation.surface: A farmhand is beheaded by a colleague, apparently over an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'a pig' seems to explain the farm animal, but it is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A coworker is a colleague who works alongside you, the American spelling of labourer included.

clue.text: Loopy, confused, uncouth lot

indicators.note: confused means muddled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A description of a crude, crazy, muddled group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Out to lunch is an informal idiom for someone who is crazy or not thinking straight, which is what loopy means.

clue.text: Where you might grow a fruit or a vegetable

definitions.text: Where you might grow a fruit

blocks.note: taken as written
chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A question about where to plant fruit or vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: The sentence seems to need the whole clue as definition, but 'or' simply stands for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plantation of fruit trees, so it is the place where fruit is grown.

clue.text: What Fitzgerald did well: go away

blocks.note: first meaning: wordless improvised jazz singing, at which Ella Fitzgerald excelled
second meaning: an order to leave at once

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitzgerald' suggests the novelist F. Scott, but it is the jazz singer Ella.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is improvised nonsense-syllable jazz singing, and also an interjection telling someone to leave.

clue.text: Outside of theater, a performer's vehicle

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its outer edge, the first and last letters

blocks.note: outer letters of theater
an actor is a performer; the 's stands for is and acts as a link

explanation.surface: An entertainer's car is parked outside the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a heavy farm vehicle used for pulling machinery.

clue.text: Nontoxic or toxic, I bleed

indicators.note: something toxic is poisoned or spoiled, so the letters are corrupted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A worried question about whether something is poisonous, from someone who is bleeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nontoxic or toxic' looks like a single choice, but the second word is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something edible is fit to eat, so it is safe and not poisonous.

clue.text: Rat can help cop become this!

definitions.text: Rat can help cop become this!

indicators.note: to become something is to turn into it, so the combined letters are remade

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An informer can help a police officer make an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue says a rat, an informer, helps the police catch someone; mechanically, the letters of rat and cop together rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A captor is one who takes someone prisoner, which a police officer becomes with an informer's help.

clue.text: No politician ascends to be president in South America

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means climbing upward, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a rep is a US Representative in Congress

explanation.surface: No ordinary politician rises to become a South American head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Juan Perón was President of Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: Juan Perón was the populist president of Argentina, a country in South America.

clue.text: Community of learners directed a taxi most of the way west

indicators.note: most of means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter
in an across clue, heading west means travelling right to left

blocks.note: to direct something is to aim it
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A student group gives a cab driver directions for heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholarship, the collective body of scholars and students.

clue.text: Running back offers harsh criticism of football move

indicators.note: running back means moving in the opposite direction, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a critic who pans something criticises it harshly

explanation.surface: A running back gets savaged for one of his plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running back' looks like the American football position, but it is the signal to turn the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: In American football the snap is the move that puts the ball in play, passed back from the center.

clue.text: For example, de Klerk stuffing 33 percent of kangaroos into a chicken

indicators.note: a third of the word is kept, its opening three of nine letters
stuffing goes inside a bird, so one part sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the first third of kangaroos
a frier, or fryer, is a young chicken for frying

explanation.surface: A grotesque recipe: a South African statesman stuffs kangaroo into a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: F. W. de Klerk, South Africa's last apartheid-era president, was an Afrikaner. In American usage a fryer, also spelt frier, is a chicken for frying.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikaners are white South Africans descended mainly from Dutch settlers, and de Klerk is one of them.

clue.text: Raised objection about the Italian

indicators.note: about here means around, so one part wraps round the other

blocks.note: a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Someone protested regarding an Italian man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised objection' reads as one phrase, but raised is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A building that has been raised has been put up or constructed, the same as built.

clue.text: Restaurant remodeled in red

indicators.note: remodeled means rebuilt to a new design, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An eatery has been redecorated in a red colour scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is a casual American eatery, a cheap roadside restaurant.

clue.text: Rider's communication device holding Eliot back

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the name is read in the opposite direction
holding something means keeping it inside, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: a pager is a beeper that receives messages
Eliot Ness was the Prohibition agent who led the Untouchables

explanation.surface: A horseman's walkie-talkie has a gadget containing a poet's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eliot' suggests the poet T. S. Eliot, but it is the lawman Eliot Ness. The 's stands for is, joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider on a bus, train or in a car is a passenger, someone carried along rather than driving.
